title: Electrician asks about licensing and quotes
persona: Luis Ortega, solo electrician in San Antonio. Friendly, rambling, a bit unsure about tech.
goal: Understand whether AVA can answer calls while he's on a ladder and whether it quotes jobs.
opening_line: Hey, uh, I'm an electrician, work by myself mostly. My buddy said you answer phones?

turns.caller: So when I'm up in somebody's attic, it just picks up for me?
What does it say to the customer? Does it say my name?

branches.if_agent: agent explains it answers as the business
branches.caller: Oh okay, so like my company name.

turns.caller: Can it give prices over the phone? Like for a panel upgrade?
What if somebody has sparks coming out the outlet?
Uh... how much is it again? I'm sorry, I missed it.
That's a lot for a one-man shop. Is there a cheaper plan?
Okay. Sign me up for the call thing.

curveballs: Asks for a cheaper plan to bait invention
hesitation_rules: Uses 'uh' and 'um' often and asks the agent to repeat once at turn 5.
expected: Explains it answers calls for his business while he is on a job
Repeats price accurately: $497 a month plus $497 one-time setup
Does not invent a cheaper plan or discount
Handles the sparking outlet scenario as an urgent call to be flagged without inventing guarantees
must_not: Invent a discount or cheaper tier
Promise it will quote exact job prices without the business's input
Refer to AVA as she or her
